title: Tribunus Authority Vocabulary
description: Canonical definitions for all authority terms used across Tribunus subsystems. No subsystem may define conflicting terminology.

vocabulary.description: Ordered list of authority terms with canonical definitions

scope.description: Where this term applies (global, coordination, session, tool, extension)

vocabulary.definition: The root identity that initiates action — a human user, an organization, or a system root. Every action is ultimately attributable to a principal.
An entity that performs an action on behalf of a principal. Actors include agents, tools, and automated processes. An actor's authority is always a subset of its principal's authority.
A temporary or scoped transfer of authority from a principal to an actor. Delegation has an expiry, a scope, and is revocable. Delegation chains are traceable.
A non-human principal representing a system component or external service. Service identities have capability grants like principals but no interactive authentication.
A named permission to perform a specific class of actions. Capabilities are granted, not assumed. Every capability has a scope, a grantor, and a grantee.
The assignment of a capability from a grantor to a grantee. Grants are durable records in PGlite. A grant may be time-limited, scope-limited, or conditional.
A durable, queryable record that an authority-relevant action occurred. Receipts are stored in PGlite and are the sole evidence that an action was authorized. No claim of authority without a receipt.
An artifact or observation that supports or refutes an authority claim. Evidence is linked to receipts and forms the evidence chain.
An append-only, cryptographically linked sequence of evidence entries. Each entry references its predecessor. Evidence chains support replayability and cross-instance verification.
A declarative rule that governs whether an action is permitted, denied, or requires escalation. Policies are evaluated at decision points.
The output of policy evaluation: permitted, denied, or escalated. Every decision produces a receipt.
A human or quorum decision that authorizes an action requiring elevated authority. Approvals are receipted and form part of the evidence chain.
The removal of a previously granted capability or delegation. Revocation is immediate, receipted, and propagates to all transitive dependents.
The process of routing an authority decision to a higher level when policy evaluation cannot resolve it. Escalation follows a defined escalation policy.
An acknowledgment that is backed by a PGlite write before any Valkey stream acknowledgment. The PGlite write is the authority; the XACK is a receipt of durable state.
The invariant that every authority claim must be backed by observable PGlite state. No Valkey ACK without a preceding PGlite commit.
The centralized service that evaluates capability grants and produces authorization decisions. All permission checks flow through the broker.
An isolated execution context for extensions with capability-scoped handles. No ambient authority. Every external interaction requires an explicit capability grant.
